intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients central to Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a local roadside stall for authentic barbacoa tacos and pulque, a traditional fermented agave drink.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from Mexico City)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of bohemian Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse the weekend artisan market, and enjoy a cup of traditional Mexican hot chocolate with churros at a local café.

experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in Roma & Condesa
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided taco crawl through the trendy Roma and Condesa neighborhoods, tasting the city's best tacos al pastor, quesadillas, and elotes (street corn) from beloved local taquerías and street carts frequented by chilangos (Mexico City locals).

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walking Tour
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture of the Palacio de Bellas Artes, view Diego Rivera's famous murals inside, then walk through the Historic Center to see the Metropolitan Cathedral, Zócalo plaza, and Templo Mayor ruins — a deep dive into Mexico's layered history.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Benito Juárez International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Take the Metro Line 5 (Terminal Aérea station) to your hotel — one of the cheapest airport transfers in the city at around 5 MXN. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, settle in, and get a good night's rest.

meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick and cheap taco from a street vendor or a 24-hour OXXO convenience store near the hotel for snacks under 50 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival at 22:30, keep Day 1 simple. Pre-download the Mexico City Metro map offline (Metro CDMX app). Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs, but use ATMs in the city for better rates. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance for late arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to the historic Centro Histórico. Walk through the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world — completely free. Explore the stunning Catedral Metropolitana (free entry to the main nave) and admire its baroque architecture. Stroll over to the Templo Mayor ruins and museum (entry ~80 MXN), an ancient Aztec temple unearthed in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco exterior for free, then walk through the nearby Alameda Central park to relax and people-watch. Visit the Museo de la Ciudad de México (entry ~30 MXN) for a deep dive into the city's fascinating history. Browse the vibrant street markets around Centro for handmade crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Barrio Chino (Chinatown) nearby or walk along Calle Regina, a pedestrian street with street performers and local vendors. Enjoy the evening atmosphere of Centro Histórico as locals gather in the plazas.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local mercado breakfast spot near the hotel — try chilaquiles or tamales with atole for around 60–80 MXN at Mercado San Juan or a nearby fondita.
meals.lunch: Grab a comida corrida (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant near Centro Histórico — typically includes soup, main dish, rice, and a drink for 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Try tacos de canasta or tacos de guisado from a street stall near Calle Regina or around the Zócalo — budget around 60–100 MXN for a filling meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes as Centro Histórico is best explored on foot. Be mindful of your belongings in crowded areas. The Metro is your best friend — a single ride costs only 5 MXN. Most major attractions open around 9–10 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online (~270 MXN) as it sells out quickly. Explore the colorful cobblestone streets and admire the colonial architecture of this artsy district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for an authentic local market experience — sample fresh tostadas, fruit, and aguas frescas for very little money. Then visit the Museo León Trotsky (entry ~50 MXN), the former home of the exiled Russian revolutionary, just a short walk from Casa Azul. Spend the rest of the afternoon exploring the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, the heart of Coyoacán.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in Coyoacán's central plaza, where street performers, artisan vendors, and locals gather. Browse the weekend craft market if visiting on a weekend. Head back to the hotel via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local panadería (bakery) in Coyoacán for fresh pan dulce and café de olla — budget around 40–60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or ceviche tostadas for around 50–80 MXN per plate. Fresh juices are also incredibly cheap here.
meals.dinner: Find a local taquería near Coyoacán or back near your hotel. Try tacos al pastor or tacos de suadero for around 15–20 MXN per taco.

day_by_day.notes: Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets online well in advance as they are frequently sold out. The neighborhood is generally safe and very tourist-friendly. Bring cash as many small vendors and market stalls do not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Chapultepec. Start with a morning walk through Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world — entry is free. Head to the Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum, entry ~95 MXN) perched atop a hill with panoramic views of the city. The murals and history inside are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-class Museo Nacional de Antropología (entry ~95 MXN), one of the best anthropology museums in the world, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and vast pre-Columbian collections. Spend at least 2–3 hours here. Afterward, stroll through the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby for window shopping and people-watching — it's free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Colonia Roma or Colonia Condesa for a vibrant evening atmosphere. These trendy neighborhoods have beautiful Art Deco architecture, tree-lined boulevards, and plenty of affordable eateries and street food options. Walk through Parque México in Condesa as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a street food stand near Chapultepec — try tortas or quesadillas for 40–60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Pack a light picnic lunch from a nearby tianguis (street market) to enjoy in Bosque de Chapultepec — fresh fruit, elotes (corn), and snacks for under 80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Eat dinner in Colonia Roma — try a local taquería or a fondita for an affordable and delicious meal. Look for places with locals eating — a strong sign of quality and value. Budget around 100–150 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec is free on Sundays for Mexican nationals, but as a tourist, the small entry fees are well worth it. The Museo Nacional de Antropología alone is worth an entire day — prioritize what interests you most. Wear sunscreen as you'll be outside for much of the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, one of the most impressive ancient sites in the Americas, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Take a bus from the Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Autobuses del Norte, Line 5) — buses run frequently and cost around 100–120 MXN round trip. Arrive early to beat the crowds and the heat. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon for breathtaking views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcoatl at Teotihuacán (site entry ~90 MXN). Browse the artisan market outside the site for affordable souvenirs — practice your bargaining skills. Head back to Mexico City by mid-afternoon bus.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening back in Mexico City doing last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela near Centro Histórico — one of the best and most affordable craft markets in the city. Enjoy a farewell dinner in the area and soak in the final moments of the city.

meals.breakfast: Eat a hearty breakfast before departing for Teotihuacán — try huevos rancheros or enfrijoladas at a local comedor near the bus terminal for 70–100 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the restaurants just outside the Teotihuacán site — look for set lunch menus (comida corrida) offering traditional Mexican dishes like mole or barbacoa for 100–150 MXN. Avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants directly at the entrance.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local restaurant near La Ciudadela or Centro Histórico. Try a traditional Mexican dish you haven't eaten yet — perhaps pozole, mole negro, or chiles en nogada if in season. Budget around 120–180 MXN for a sit-down meal.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Teotihuacán trip as early as possible (aim to leave by 7–8 AM) to avoid heat and crowds. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a hat — there is very little shade at the site. Wear sturdy shoes for climbing the pyramids. The site is large, so plan to spend 3–4 hours. Keep a small budget reserve for last-minute souvenirs and tips.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is at 22:30. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take an authorized airport taxi or pre-booked ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and grab a light snack nearby if needed before resting.

meals.dinner: Quick late-night bite near the hotel — look for a 24-hour taqueria or convenience store snack to tide you over until morning.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is arrival only. No activities are scheduled before 22:30. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon landing. Keep some Mexican pesos (MXN) handy for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head to the historic Centro Histórico. Visit the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Explore the Metropolitan Cathedral and walk around the surrounding colonial architecture. Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its museum to learn about the ancient Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history. Stroll through the pedestrian streets of Madero and browse local artisan shops. Head to the Mercado de Artesanías or Mercado Ciudadela for affordable, authentic Mexican crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Garibaldi Plaza in the early evening where mariachi bands perform. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and street performances. Wind down with a relaxed dinner at a traditional Mexican restaurant in Centro.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros, a classic Mexican morning staple (budget ~150–200 MXN).
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba — a historic and beloved Mexico City restaurant in Centro Histórico serving traditional Mexican cuisine at mid-range prices (budget ~200–350 MXN).
meals.dinner: El Cardenal — an iconic restaurant near the Zócalo known for authentic regional Mexican dishes and mole. Great value for quality (budget ~300–450 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico involves a lot of walking on cobblestones. Templo Mayor charges a small entrance fee (~80 MXN). Palacio Nacional is free. The area is busiest on weekdays, so expect some crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the floating gardens of Xochimilco, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Board a colorful trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) and float through the ancient canals surrounded by lush greenery. Vendors on smaller boats will paddle up selling food, drinks, and flowers — a truly unique local experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head north to the Coyoacán neighborhood, one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian districts. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) — the famous blue house where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book tickets in advance online. Stroll through Coyoacán's tree-lined streets, plazas, and artisan markets.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the relaxed evening atmosphere in Coyoacán's central plaza, Jardín Centenario. Watch street performers, browse local stalls, and soak in the neighborhood vibe. Head back toward the hotel area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local mercado near the hotel — try tamales and atole, a traditional morning combination popular with locals (budget ~80–120 MXN).
meals.lunch: Eat lunch at a traditional comida corrida (set lunch) restaurant in Coyoacán — a multi-course affordable meal typical of Mexican lunch culture (budget ~150–250 MXN).
meals.dinner: Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — a stylish restaurant with excellent Oaxacan-inspired Mexican cuisine and mezcal selections (budget ~350–500 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets online well in advance as they sell out quickly (~270 MXN). Xochimilco is best visited on weekends when it's most festive, but weekdays are less crowded. Budget for trajinera rental (~300–500 MXN per boat, shared among a group).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec Park — one of the greatest museums in Latin America. Spend 2–3 hours exploring its vast collection of pre-Columbian artifacts, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. The museum alone is worth a half-day visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chapultepec Park, the massive urban green space often called the 'lungs of Mexico City.' Walk through the park, visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched on a hill with panoramic views of the city, and explore its exhibits on Mexican history. Afterward, head to the trendy Polanco neighborhood for upscale shopping and people-watching along Presidente Masaryk Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Condesa or Roma neighborhoods — two of Mexico City's hippest districts filled with Art Deco architecture, tree-lined boulevards, independent cafés, bars, and restaurants. Enjoy a leisurely evening stroll and settle in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Roma or Condesa — try a local brunch spot with avocado toast, fresh juices, and Mexican pastries (pan dulce) (budget ~150–250 MXN).
meals.lunch: Quick and delicious street tacos near Chapultepec Park — al pastor, carnitas, or suadero from a reputable street taco stand (budget ~80–150 MXN).
meals.dinner: Contramar in Colonia Roma — a beloved seafood-focused restaurant famous for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. A Mexico City institution (budget ~400–600 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Museo Nacional de Antropología entrance fee is ~85 MXN (free on Sundays for Mexican nationals). Chapultepec Castle charges ~85 MXN. Both are closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. Polanco is upscale; window shopping is free and enjoyable.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning day trip to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City (roughly 1 hour by bus from the Terminal Norte). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon for sweeping views of this extraordinary archaeological site. Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop by the Mercado de Jamaica — Mexico City's famous flower market — for a colorful and fragrant local experience. Pick up some fresh flowers or exotic tropical blooms as a memorable local encounter. Spend the remaining afternoon relaxing or doing any last-minute souvenir shopping in the Mercado de Artesanías.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in the Roma Norte neighborhood. Explore its vibrant bar and restaurant scene, enjoy a mezcal or craft cocktail at a local mezcalería, and reflect on the week's adventures over a memorable farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Teotihuacán — fuel up with a hearty meal for the pyramid climb.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the restaurants near the Teotihuacán site entrance — try the traditional barbacoa (slow-cooked meat) which is a regional specialty of the State of Mexico (budget ~200–300 MXN).
meals.dinner: Máximo Bistrot in Roma Norte — a farm-to-table restaurant celebrating local Mexican ingredients with creative, seasonal dishes. A perfect farewell dinner (budget ~450–650 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Buses to Teotihuacán depart regularly from Terminal Norte (Autobuses del Norte metro station) — round trip costs approximately ~100 MXN. Entrance to the archaeological zone is ~80 MXN. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring water — the site is largely open and exposed to the sun. Start no later than 8:00 AM to maximize your time there.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late-night arrival. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort after landing at 22:30.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night welcome: After check-in, unwind at the hotel's rooftop bar or lounge. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and light bites from the in-house menu. Take in the ambient city lights and decompress from your journey.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining prior to arrival
meals.dinner: Late-night in-hotel dining: Order from the resort's 24-hour room service menu — recommended: a premium charcuterie board, guacamole with house-made tortilla chips, and a glass of top-shelf mezcal to begin your Mexico City experience authentically.

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and private transfer to the hotel. Pre-arrange a luxury private car transfer (e.g., black SUV) from Benito Juárez International Airport to the resort for a seamless arrival experience. No activities are scheduled for this evening beyond check-in and relaxation.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Afterward, take a private guided tour of the historic Centro Histórico, including the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral (Catedral Metropolitana), and the ancient ruins of Templo Mayor. A knowledgeable private guide will provide rich cultural and historical context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's legendary murals depicting Mexican history — a breathtaking cultural highlight. Continue to the nearby Mercado de San Juan, a premium gourmet market beloved by locals and chefs, where you can sample artisan cheeses, exotic fruits, fine charcuterie, and imported delicacies. Browse at your leisure with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Polanco neighborhood for a world-class dinner. After dinner, take a private evening stroll through Polanco's elegant streets and boutique-lined avenues before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel gourmet breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platters, eggs to order, and artisan Mexican coffee or champagne.
meals.lunch: Casual premium tasting lunch at Mercado de San Juan — curated bites of local cheeses, cured meats, fresh ceviche, and craft beverages sourced directly from market vendors.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol (Polanco) — one of Latin America's most celebrated restaurants by Chef Enrique Olvera. Indulge in the legendary Mole Madre tasting menu, a pinnacle of modern Mexican haute cuisine. Reservations essential and strongly recommended well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor and Palacio Nacional are within walking distance of each other in Centro Histórico. Private car and guide recommended throughout the day for comfort and efficiency. Dress smart-casual for dinner at Pujol. Confirm Pujol reservations before departure from home.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private half-day excursion to the ancient Aztec pyramids of Teotihuacán, located approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Arrive early (before the crowds) with your private guide and luxury transport. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and explore the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. Your guide will bring the ancient civilization vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and spend the afternoon in the bohemian, artsy neighborhood of Coyoacán. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul) — the iconic blue house where the legendary painter was born and lived. Stroll through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets, browse artisan markets, and soak up the vibrant local culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Condesa or Roma neighborhood for cocktails at a celebrated mezcalería, followed by a refined dinner at one of Mexico City's top contemporary restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure — light and energizing: Greek yogurt, seasonal fruit, avocado toast, and cold-brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Al fresco lunch at a premium restaurant in Coyoacán — try Corazón de Maguey for elevated traditional Mexican cuisine in a beautiful courtyard setting, featuring dishes like duck in mole negro and artisan mezcal pairings.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (Colonia Roma) — an iconic Mexico City seafood institution beloved by locals and international food lovers alike. Must-try: the signature tuna tostadas and grilled fish 'a la talla' with red and green salsa. Pair with a premium natural wine or house margarita.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat crowds and midday heat. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection. The site involves significant walking and stair climbing. Private luxury SUV with a bilingual expert guide is highly recommended for the full day. Book La Casa Azul tickets in advance as they sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the morning with a private art and culture immersion at the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec. One of the greatest museums in the world, it houses extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts including the legendary Aztec Sun Stone. A private docent guide will make the experience deeply enriching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the lush Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — one of the largest urban parks in the Western Hemisphere. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched atop the hill, offering panoramic views of the city and housing Mexico's National History Museum. Afterward, head into Polanco for luxury shopping along Presidente Masaryk Avenue — Mexico City's answer to the Champs-Élysées — featuring Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Cartier, and top local designers.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Mexico City's vibrant nightlife and fine dining scene with a reservation at one of the city's most exclusive rooftop dining venues, followed by cocktails at a premier speakeasy-style bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — indulge in a full à la carte menu: huevos rancheros prepared with heirloom salsa, fresh-squeezed juices, and artisan pan dulce.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quintonil (Polanco) — Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant focusing on seasonal, locally sourced Mexican ingredients with a sophisticated modern approach. Ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants. Opt for the full tasting menu for the complete experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dulce Patria (Polanco) — Chef Martha Ortiz's visually stunning and theatrically presented modern Mexican cuisine. Known for its bold flavors, artistic plating, and vibrant atmosphere. A true celebration of Mexican culture through food.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Anthropology and Chapultepec Castle are both within Chapultepec Park — plan 2–3 hours for the museum alone. Private guide for the museum is highly recommended. Polanco is directly adjacent to Chapultepec, making afternoon transitions seamless. Confirm all restaurant reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic private boat tour through the ancient canals of Xochimilco — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Mexico City's most unique and beloved cultural experiences. Rent a private 'trajinera' (colorful flat-bottomed boat) decorated with flowers, and glide through the historic waterways. Enjoy mariachi music, floating market vendors, and the lush, tranquil surroundings — a vivid contrast to the urban energy of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Museo Dolores Olmedo, a stunning hacienda-style museum set in beautiful gardens, housing an extraordinary collection of works by Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo in an intimate, peaceful setting — far less crowded than other art destinations. Afterward, return to the hotel for a relaxing afternoon: enjoy a premium spa treatment, rooftop pool, or simply rest and pack for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final night in Mexico City — celebrate the journey with a grand farewell dinner at one of the city's most iconic and atmospheric fine dining establishments. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a premium bottle of Mexican wine or a flight of artisan mezcals.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely champagne breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon, freshly baked croissants, premium cheeses, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine to start the final day in style.
meals.lunch: Floating brunch on the trajinera in Xochimilco — arrange for a private catered spread of traditional Mexican dishes: tamales, quesadillas, fresh fruit, and agua fresca or micheladas served aboard your private boat.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Rosetta (Colonia Roma) — Chef Elena Reygadas' flagship restaurant, winner of Latin America's Best Female Chef. Set in a beautifully restored colonial mansion, Rosetta offers an exquisite menu blending Italian and Mexican culinary traditions with hyper-seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. An elegant and memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is approximately 25–30 km south of the city center — allow 45–60 minutes travel time each way. Book a private trajinera in advance for the most comfortable and exclusive experience. Museo Dolores Olmedo is very close to Xochimilco, making it an ideal pairing. Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge — arrange a luxury private transfer to the airport if departing the following morning. Tip generously for outstanding service throughout the trip.
